title: Build assembly alignment chains and project annotations

sources.locator: sections I-V; same-organism and other-organism lift guidelines

scientific_use: Construct assembly-to-assembly alignments and chain/net files, select single-coverage chains, and use a chain file to transfer gene annotations between assemblies. The example explicitly retrieves an ensGene genePred table, runs liftOver -genePred, and writes mapped and unmapped genePred outputs.
tool_role_basis: The documented workflow composes existing faSplit, BLAT, axtChain, chainNet, chainNetSubset, liftOver and database-export tools; it does not implement their algorithms.

inputs.meaning: Old and new genome assemblies, with the new assembly aligned against the old assembly; later, an old-assembly genePred annotation table.
inputs.format: FASTA/nib genome inputs, PSL alignments, chain/net intermediate files, genePred annotation

outputs.meaning: Coordinate mappings between assemblies and projected gene annotations; unmapped annotation records are retained separately.
outputs.stage: derived assembly alignment and projected annotations

dependencies: Kent command-line tools faSplit, BLAT, liftUp, axtChain, chainMergeSort, chainSplit, chainNet, netChainSubset, liftOver, and a database export client
Assembly FASTA/nib sources, chrom sizes, cluster/local scratch paths, and a prebuilt database annotation table
The guide uses historical hg12-era paths and cluster commands; modern execution setup is not provided.
evidence: src/hg/doc/liftOver.txt: chain naming and same-organism workflow; BLAT -> axtChain -> chainNet -> chainNetSubset; section V runs liftOver -genePred and emits new.gp plus unmapped.gp
limitations: Guide itself warns that its instructions were not tested and recommends running one step at a time.
The example is historical and uses cluster-specific paths and assembly identifiers; suitable modern input assemblies and chain availability must be established.
Cross-species chains are explicitly said to be inadequate for homology mapping without other tools and human intervention.

title: Summarize bigWig signal over BED intervals

sources.locator: usage() options and bigWigAverageOverBed(), averageFetchingEachBlock(), averageFetchingEachChrom()

scientific_use: Compute per-feature coverage and signal summaries for BED intervals from a bigWig track. BED12 block structure lets a task summarize exon blocks while skipping introns; optional center-window sampling, min/max, BED echo with appended means, and overall statistics extend the output.
tool_role_basis: The source implements a callable existing command; the unit is using it to summarize genome-wide signal, not changing its algorithm.

inputs.meaning: Numeric genomic signal aligned to a genome assembly
Named genomic regions; BED12 block coordinates are used for block-aware features

outputs.meaning: Per-region total size, covered bases, sum, mean with uncovered bases treated as zero (mean0), and mean over covered bases; optional min/max, augmented BED, and global stats
outputs.format: tab-delimited table; optional BED and RA files

dependencies: Kent bigWig and BED libraries; compatible chromosome naming and genome assembly between the bigWig and BED
Input BED names must be unique; source switches from interval queries to chromosome-at-a-time processing at 3000 blocks.
evidence: src/utils/bigWigAverageOverBed/bigWigAverageOverBed.c: usage() documents input and output columns/options
same source: checkUniqueNames(), block-aware interval aggregation, missing chromosomes treated as zero, thresholded block/chromosome strategies
limitations: No biological example or named signal dataset was identified in the inspected source.
Assembly compatibility and handling of out-of-range BED intervals should be resolved during authoring.
Performance depends on input block count and chromosome sizes; no execution or runtime measurement was performed.

title: Filter and recode VCF alternate alleles
scientific_use: Remove variants at positions in an exclusion VCF, remove alternate alleles below a minimum count, update AC/AN and genotype allele codes when genotypes are present, and optionally rename variants from REF, POS and retained ALT alleles. Regression recipes cover genotype and no-genotype paths and coordinate exclusion.
tool_role_basis: The inspected C program is an existing VCF-processing command; the task would apply it to variant data rather than implement the filtering algorithm.

inputs.meaning: Variant records and optional site positions to exclude; for genotype-bearing VCF, allele counts are calculated from genotypes and incoming AC/AN are not trusted

outputs.meaning: Filtered VCF with remaining alternate alleles, updated allele counts and recoded genotype indices, or unchanged header plus filtered records

dependencies: Kent C libraries and compiled vcfFilter executable
When -excludeVcf is used, CHROM values in both files must match; VCF sample-column counts must be consistent.
evidence: src/utils/vcfFilter/vcfFilter.c: usage text, genotype versus INFO AC behavior, exclude-position hash, allele sorting/recode and output logic
src/utils/vcfFilter/tests/makefile: six regression scenarios compare generated VCF with expected outputs
src/utils/vcfFilter/tests/input/subset.vcf: headers identify VCFv4.2, NC_045512v2 and faToVcf provenance
src/utils/vcfFilter/tests/input/exclude.vcf: source comment identifies a SARS-CoV-2 masking-strategies webpage and selected exclusion annotations
limitations: The checked-in VCF is a small regression input and its original upstream variant-call dataset/accession is not identified by the inspected files.
The exclusion VCF is a hand-selected list; the full selection rationale and redistribution terms are unresolved.
The min-allele-count threshold is not equivalent to a cohort-level frequency filter unless sample composition and ploidy are understood.
Source inspection and fixture metadata do not establish successful execution on a production VCF.

title: Query, intersect and export Genome Browser tables

sources.locator: Guided Walkthrough steps 1-6; Optional: filter, subset, or combine tracks

scientific_use: Select a genome assembly, hosted annotation track/table and genomic region or identifier list; filter rows, intersect with another track, and export chosen fields, BED/GTF, custom track, sequence or summary statistics. The tutorial names questions such as SNPs overlapping RefSeq coding exons and genomic regions overlapping peaks.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial documents querying and composing existing Genome Browser data and Table Browser operations, not implementing those tools.

inputs.meaning: Assembly plus one or more hosted track tables and optional loci, gene identifiers, filters, or second overlap track
inputs.format: UCSC Genome Browser assembly/table selections, genomic coordinates and identifier lists
inputs.stage: hosted reference annotations or user-defined regions

outputs.meaning: Filtered/intersected rows or sequence and optional descriptive statistics
outputs.format: table, BED, GTF, custom track or sequence output

dependencies: Accessible UCSC Genome Browser/Table Browser instance and chosen assembly tracks
Track/table schemas and joinable fields; tutorial notes whole-genome output may be unavailable for large tracks.
evidence: docs/tutorials/tableBrowserTutorial.md: steps 1-6 describe assembly, track, table, region, output format and query submission
same tutorial: filter and intersection examples explicitly mention SNP coding-exon overlap and peaks intersecting regions
limitations: No specific track or assembly-backed observation dataset is selected by the tutorial; dataset_ids remain empty.
Hosted track contents and availability vary by assembly and time; output reproducibility requires pinning assembly, track/table versions and query settings.
Rendered tutorial references interactive tutorial URLs that were not opened; only repository Markdown text was inspected.
